from solution import group_tuples


def test_issue_example_given():
    """Example: [('x','y'),('x','z'),('w','t')] groups to [('x','y','z'),('w','t')]."""
    result = group_tuples([('x', 'y'), ('x', 'z'), ('w', 't')])
    expected = [('x', 'y', 'z'), ('w', 't')]  # 2 with 'x' -> 1 + 2 = 3 items; 1 with 'w' -> 2 items; 3 inputs -> 2 groups
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_empty_input():
    """Empty input has no common first element so returns empty list."""
    result = group_tuples([])
    expected = []  # 0 inputs -> 0 groups; 0 == 0
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_single_tuple():
    """Single tuple forms one group unchanged."""
    result = group_tuples([('w', 't')])
    expected = [('w', 't')]  # 1 input -> 1 group; 1 == 1
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_distinct_first_elements():
    """Tuples with distinct first elements stay as separate groups."""
    result = group_tuples([('a', '1'), ('b', '2'), ('c', '3')])
    expected = [('a', '1'), ('b', '2'), ('c', '3')]  # 3 inputs, 3 distinct keys -> 3 groups; 3 == 3
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_all_same_first_element():
    """All tuples sharing one first element merge into one tuple."""
    result = group_tuples([('x', 'a'), ('x', 'b'), ('x', 'c')])
    expected = [('x', 'a', 'b', 'c')]  # 3 inputs, 1 key -> 1 group; 1 + 3 = 4 items
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_nonadjacent_keys_merge():
    """Same first elements merge even when not adjacent in input."""
    result = group_tuples([('a', '1'), ('b', '2'), ('a', '3'), ('b', '4')])
    expected = [('a', '1', '3'), ('b', '2', '4')]  # 4 inputs, 2 keys x 2 each -> 2 groups; 1 + 2 = 3 items each
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_group_order_follows_first_seen():
    """Output group order follows first appearance of each key."""
    result = group_tuples([('w', 't'), ('x', 'y'), ('x', 'z')])
    expected = [('w', 't'), ('x', 'y', 'z')]  # 3 inputs -> 2 groups; 'w' at index 0 first, 'x' at index 1 second; 1 + 1 = 2 groups
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_value_order_follows_appearance():
    """Values inside a merged group follow order of appearance."""
    result = group_tuples([('x', 'z'), ('x', 'y')])
    expected = [('x', 'z', 'y')]  # 2 inputs, 1 key -> 1 group; 1 + 2 = 3 items with 'z' before 'y'
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_numeric_first_elements():
    """Non-string first elements group by equality like strings do."""
    result = group_tuples([(1, 'a'), (1, 'b'), (2, 'c')])
    expected = [(1, 'a', 'b'), (2, 'c')]  # 3 inputs -> 2 groups; key 1: 1 + 2 = 3 items, key 2: 2 items
    assert result == expected


def test_issue_mixed_counts_three_keys():
    """Multiple keys with different counts each form one group per key."""
    result = group_tuples([('a', '1'), ('b', '2'), ('a', '3'), ('c', '4'), ('b', '5'), ('b', '6')])
    expected = [('a', '1', '3'), ('b', '2', '5', '6'), ('c', '4')]  # counts a:2 -> 1 + 2 = 3 items, b:3 -> 1 + 3 = 4 items, c:1 -> 2 items; 6 inputs -> 3 groups
    assert result == expected


def test_contract_takes_single_argument():
    """Public interface defines group_tuples(Input) with one parameter."""
    import inspect
    expected_params = 1  # group_tuples(Input) -> 1 param; 1 == 1
    assert len(inspect.signature(group_tuples).parameters) == expected_params


def test_contract_groups_are_tuples():
    """Public interface example shows groups as tuples inside a list."""
    result = group_tuples([('a', '1'), ('a', '2')])
    expected_count = 1  # 2 inputs with 1 key -> 1 group; 1 + 2 = 3 items; 1 == 1
    assert len(result) == expected_count and all(type(g) is tuple for g in result)
